Use rsyslog to add hostname as a prefix to messages
output: echo 'template(name="WithHost" type="string" string="%HOSTNAME%: %msg%\n")' > /etc/rsyslog.d/host_prefix.conf && echo '*.* action(type="omfile" template="WithHost")' >> /etc/rsyslog.d/host_prefix.conf

instruction: Create syslog-ng source for TCP with TLS and client auth
output: echo 'source s_tls_client { tcp(ip("0.0.0.0") port(6514) tls(key_file("/etc/ssl/private/syslog.key") cert_file("/etc/ssl/certs/syslog.crt") peer_verify("optional-untrusted") ca_dir("/etc/ssl/certs"))); };' >> /etc/syslog-ng/conf.d/tls_client.conf

Create syslog-ng log path with fallback destination
output: echo 'destination d_primary { tcp("192.168.1.100" port(514)); };' >> /etc/syslog-ng/conf.d/fallback.conf && echo 'destination d_fallback { file("/var/log/local_buffer"); };' >> /etc/syslog-ng/conf.d/fallback.conf && echo 'log { source(s_sys); destination(d_primary); destination(d_fallback); flags(fallback); };' >> /etc/syslog-ng/conf.d/fallback.conf

instruction: Set up rsyslog to convert syslog to GELF format
output: echo 'template(name="GELF" type="list") { constant(value="{\"version\":\"1.1\",\"host\":\"") property(name="hostname") constant(value="\",\"short_message\":\"") property(name="msg") constant(value="\"}\n"); };' > /etc/rsyslog.d/gelf.conf
